newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government securities end narrowly mixed.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government securities end narrowly mixed.

text.p: Singapore government securities ended narrowly mixed in moderate trade on interbank and retail interest, dealers said on Friday.

"The interbank rate rose slightly again today but there was still little impact on the market. Treasury bill yields were slightly lower but bond prices were narrowly mixed. Volume was moderate," a local dealer said.
In treasury bills, three-months ended at a yield of 0.88/0.83 percent compared with Thursday's yield of 0.93/0.88 percent and one-year at a yield of 1.38/1.33 percent against 1.43/1.38 percent.
Among bonds, July 1998 closed at S$99.30/99.35 from Thursday's close of S$99.25/99.30, September 2001 at S$97.27/97.32 versus S$97.38/97.43 and June 2003 at S$95.27/95.32 against S$95.38/95.43.
The overnight interbank offered rate rose to 3-9/16 3-7/16 percent from Thursday's 3-7/16 3-5/16 percent.
